intro: Above the travertines of Pamukkale, in Denizli province, lies a city of healing and of the dead. This is Hierapolis, whose story begins in the 2nd century BC: a spa and a necropolis city in one.
history: Hierapolis was founded by the kings of Pergamon, and its hot springs made it a centre of healing. Earthquakes destroyed it, but the city rose again, rebuilt in grand Roman style.
structure-2: You are now at the Theatre, cut into the slope above the travertines of Pamukkale. It held 15,000 spectators. Look at the stage front: three ranks of columns deep, it survives in large part and was re-erected between 2004 and 2014. Pause for a moment and imagine every seat filled.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Antique Pool, the Necropolis, Frontinus Street and the Temple of Apollo.
facts: Did you know? The columns lying in the Antique Pool fell there during an earthquake in the 7th century. Then there is the Plutonion, the 'Gate to Hell', which leaks carbon dioxide from below. Sacrificial animals died there while the priests survived, because the gas pools at ground level, leaving a standing man's head above the cloud. The necropolis, with more than 1,200 tombs, is the largest in Anatolia. Many who came to the hot springs for a cure never left.
outro: This brings our journey through Hierapolis to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
